en: The Secret Essential Abridged Method for the Sequential Recitation of the Universal Sovereign Cakravartin King of Wish-Fulfilling Mani Jewels,
translated by Drolé Sengé.
I shall now explain the method of contemplation: The three types of mantras are applied in succession.
First, employ the Great Mind for external empowerment; Second, the Root Mantra while visualizing internally;
Third, the Small Mind for both internal and external. One should maintain focused attention without confusion.
Thus, these three paths of wondrous mantras establish the practitioner on the ground of the Vidyārāja.
If one practices this samaya, one must possess seven kinds of sublime characteristics,
just as a Wheel-Turning King who possesses the seven treasures rules over the four continents and brings them all under his command.
Next, the methods for conforming to various recitations are explained:
Furthermore, one should select a pure and auspicious location—whether in the mountains or by a pond, or in a monastery’s meditation cell, or within a stupa containing the Buddha’s relics.
One should apply the mind with diligence to prepare all the necessary requisites.
First, one should uphold the *Dhāraṇī* according to the instructions; next, the practitioner must personally arrange their own seat.
With the Honored One facing west before them, the practitioner sits facing east in front of the image.
Having bathed for purification, they should anoint their body with incense.
Furthermore, don new, clean, and exquisite garments, and carry various implements for offering.

At every step, visualize an eight-petaled lotus flower. Contemplate transforming the ground so it is free from impurities, perform the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) to protect the body, and enter the sanctum.
Place [the image] before you and perform the recitation.
First, using the Great Heart Mantra King, bathe and purify yourself;
recite the protection-binding dhāraṇī to sprinkle water upon your body and consecrate your robes. Furthermore, one must visualize that all things are accomplished.
Thus, these five types [of rites] are performed in successive order, employing both the Great Vidyā and their respective mudrās.
Oṃ padma-jvāla-maṇi mahājvāla hūṃ. [Recite this] seven times for each of the bathing implements.
Thereafter, perform the ablution.
Visualize the water as white, like nectar. Furthermore, visualize your own body as defiled by impurities and afflictions;
once this water has been received, all dust and toil shall fall away entirely. Having finished the bath, you must wash yourself clean.
Take a small amount of earth, empower it seven times, and wash yourself clean at the appropriate time;
then, when putting on your clothes, empower them likewise seven times while forming this visualization.
I now take this body and don the vajra armor. Having completed the ritual according to the dharma, one must immediately sprinkle the body with water;
taking a handful of water, empower it seven times and scatter it over the body.
Visualize that from the midst of space, a rain of various precious flowers falls.
When pervading the entire world, one must protect the body.
Form this secret mudrā and recite it seven times; seal the seven locations—the heart, the two shoulders, the two eyes, and the two knees—and finally release it over the head.
Having also accomplished the great protection of the body, one must then perform the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
If binding the altar-boundary, one should open four gates; otherwise, one should not bind the boundary.
If one performs the rites of binding and protection, one must in all cases apply the mind and arrange the sequence of the ritual implements before performing the acts of invocation and so forth.
Furthermore, the fundamental ritual manual is explained: visualize and invoke the Great Holy King.
Recite this secret mantra and form the mudrā;
visualizing yourself going to that mountain one by one, remain focused on prostrating and making the invitation.
Lead the Venerable One into the maṇḍala, and again offer argha water, as well as incense, flowers, food, and ointments.
With lamp-shades, banners, streamers, medicinal substances, and so forth, make offerings to that Vidyārāja according to the ritual.
Having performed the visualization and made offerings to the Noble One, hold the rosary as appropriate and recite the secret mantra.
Repent of past transgressions and make aspirational prayers; then, sitting upright with sincere devotion, contemplate the Vidyārāja.
The practitioner sits upright in front of the image and contemplates.
With focused attention, they clearly visualize Mount Potalaka, adorned with various jewels and abounding in flowers and fruits.
Upon its summit is the palace of the Noble One, which is situated therein.
One should visualize the Noble One seated within the palace,
his body adorned with exquisite and wondrous offerings. The practitioner, from within this mental visualization,
proceeds to that mountain to welcome the Venerable One by reciting his name, and leads him into the ritual arena.
In the center of the maṇḍala, upon the lotus pedestal, one should install the Noble One and then offer arghya water.
This should be placed in a new copper vessel or, alternatively, a white porcelain vessel filled with scented water.
Having offered [the water] to the Noble One, one should then recite the mantra.
Furthermore, one should visualize that the Noble One has accepted this water and sprinkled it everywhere in the four directions, as well as upon one’s own sublime body;
the practitioner should contemplate minutely as the Honored One sprinkles the water.
The trichiliocosm is like lapis lazuli, transparent inside and out, with not a single thing within it.
Having offered the *argha* water, one next makes offerings of incense, flowers, food and drink,
unguents, powdered incense, lamps, and canopies, consecrating each one individually.
Having completed the offerings of mantras and mudrās,
one should, before the noble deity, repent for one’s physical transgressions and reproach one’s own faults. Thereafter,
one should again make aspirations, setting forth all that is sought according to one’s heart.
Within that visualization, construct a mandala with three gates, leaving only the western gate open;
then, demarcate the great boundary (mahā-sīmā) outside the body in the four directions, extending all around to the limits of the realm of space.
Next, using fragrant unguents, smear them upon your arms.
Thereafter, while reciting, hold the *akṣamālā* (rosary) and fumigate it with incense.
Joining the two hands in *añjali*, place them three times upon the crown of the head and speak these words:
"I keep this in mind; I serve the Noble One; I uphold this secret mantra."
I only pray that the Venerable One, not forsaking great compassion,
shall not violate his original vow but shall swiftly manifest a body of all wondrous adornments;
having seen it, may I immediately realize the stage of the Cloud of Dharma.
Constantly attending the Venerable One, never departing from his side,
having made this vow, he then recited the root secret mantra, saying: *Namo āratna-tārāye*.
Namaḥ āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā...
TA-ṬA-HE AṢṬĀṆA NAVAKṢARĀVATI JÑĀTAMANI MAHĀPĀNMA RU-RU TIṢṬHA JVALA AKRĀŚAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Recite this mantra, *svāhā*,
for three hundred thousand times over the course of seven days;
the Noble One will then manifest before the practitioner.
Whatever one seeks according to one's heart's desire shall all be accomplished.
If one constantly maintains this recitation, three times each day,
reciting it one thousand and eight times— or one hundred and eight times— for each session, until such a number is fulfilled.
Recite three hundred thousand times, and you will immediately attain siddhi.
At each session, perform the rites of welcoming and sending away, and the dharma of entrustment and so forth.
The great-mind secret mantra says:
Furthermore, it is said that the most supreme King of Small Minds can accomplish all *siddhis*.
By employing the three karmas together and binding the wondrous mudrās, one recites the secret mantra and offers the entrustment.
Moreover, within the visualization, one removes the boundary (*sīmābandha*) and next offers *argha* water to the four directions.
Afterward, having reproached oneself for past transgressions and felt deep shame and remorse, one should escort the Great Sage back to his original palace and install the Venerable One in that hall.
Having bid farewell, one should reflect upon returning to one's own region.
Furthermore, the practitioner, after each recitation, must perform the entrustment.
Having bound this secret mudrā and recited the mantra, he entrusted it to the Noble One with these words:
"The required number of recitations and the effort of its practice are hereby entrusted to you, O Venerable One; we pray that you accept and protect them."
Do not allow it to be lost or scattered. Furthermore, visualize the hand-seal (*mudrā*) as being like a treasure-store that pervades all things;
place it within the treasury. Having bestowed it upon the Noble One, and the Noble One having accepted it, place it within a lotus flower. Thus, complete the act of entrustment.
One must also repent and make great vows; thereafter, the holy one returns to his palace.
Regarding the method for escorting him: first, the boundary (*sīmā*) is removed, then fragrant water is taken and sprinkled in the four directions, as well as offered to the holy one.

Then, one should escort [the deity] away; again forming the secret mudrā and reciting the mantra, while further visualizing oneself, one escorts the holy one back to his own palace and installs him within the hall.
Once the holy one is seated, one must take one's leave.
Returning to one's original position, one should recite the secret mantra with careful attention:
Oṃ varadābhayaṃ hūṃ. I shall now describe the characteristics of the secret mudrā associated with this.
First, when forming the Great Seal (mahāmudrā), apply various types of fragrant ointments to the arms.
Then, bind the seal, placing it upon the crown of the head, at the heart, and with palms joined;
[join] the two little fingers and the two ring fingers.
The hook is held in the palm.
The two index fingers press upon the second joints on the backs of the middle fingers.
The two thumbs are held upright side by side.
This is the mantra and mudrā of the Great Mind; they must be employed together for the empowerment to be performed.
Recite each secret word seven times and seal them with their respective mudrās.
Whether casting [the flower] or remaining [in place], one must visualize its successful accomplishment.
Each and every [action] shall be in accordance with the Dharma; one must not, in the midst of these, allow the mind to take other objects as its focus or to conform to worldly ways.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, remain settled within the profound realm of all Buddhas.
If there are practitioners who cultivate this Dharma:
Before long, one shall accomplish the Wisdom of All Modes (sarvākārajñatā).
Regarding the second root mantra-seal of the second root mantra: join the wrists of both hands together.
It should be held at the chest.
The ten fingers are spread apart;
the two little fingers and the two thumbs are both extended upward, resembling the shape of a lotus flower.
One should likewise seal and stabilize it according to the previous method;
there is only the movement of the thumbs for the invitation.
Third, the mudrā for the mantra of the Minor Heart: with both hands, join the palms hollowly, like a lotus flower that has not yet opened.
If, at the time of entrustment, one maintains the aforementioned visualization and dispatches the Venerable One by opening the two thumbs,
this small-finger secret mudrā may be employed for all matters throughout the Lotus Family.
I now briefly set forth this secret and profound sequence of recitation within the samaya of the Great Lotus Family.
The practitioner must not transmit it erroneously, guarding it as one would one's own eyes.
If one can act in this way,
all the noble ones will rejoice greatly and keep that person in mind;
all the benevolent deities will constantly protect them day and night, never departing from their side.
Now, following the Lotus Family, I shall briefly explain the wish-fulfilling jewel wheel, the most secret and supreme among all families.
There are four types of characteristics for the recitation that accomplishes both mundane and supramundane dharmas; listen attentively as I describe them.
First is the rite of pacification (*śāntika*); second, the accomplishment of increasing merit and wisdom (*pauṣṭika*);
third, the method for fulfilling one's heart's desires (*vaśya*); and fourth, the subjugation of all enemies (*abhicāruka*).
These four types of homa rites are set forth here in their sequence of superior, middling, and inferior methods.
If you wish to accomplish the rite of pacifying calamities, first generate a mind of patience and compassion;
you must seek the stage of unsurpassed, wondrous enlightenment and take no pleasure in the minds of the Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha vehicles.
Furthermore, if you seek to accomplish great matters, you must first perform the method for transforming obstacles.
Furthermore, take sixteen finger-widths of white sandalwood;
hold one piece and burn one, reciting your own name one hundred and eight or one thousand and eight times. All original aspirations will be fulfilled.
If the practitioner removes the illnesses of others, or extinguishes great calamities and misfortunes within a nation, [the same shall apply].
Whether for calamities befalling oneself or others, or for the sake of animals, one should apply the mind to invite the Great Sage.
At each and every great city gate, one should visualize the respective Root Vidyārāja seated there, adorned with various exquisite jewels.
One should contemplate his six arms exactly as they have been described.

Again, visualize a white light emerging from between the eyebrows; slowly and extensively drawing it forth, it pervades the world, and all the calamities of every sentient being are instantly and completely extinguished until nothing remains.
Or, visualize this light entering one's own body, whereby all karmic obstacles and transgressions are utterly annihilated.
Through empowerment, sins are extinguished and merit is born; by further diligent recitation, one attains accomplishment.
Now I shall briefly explain this method for generating merit.
Out of great compassion, the Bodhisattva manifests emanations throughout all realms in accordance with sentient beings, following the inclinations of those beings' hearts.
Furthermore, he establishes various treasuries of teachings, with diverse Dharma gates each distinct;
those followed in hundreds of thousands of lands all achieve their goals through diligent seeking.
Whether teaching the dharma of marks or the markless, he accords with the inclinations and natures of sentient beings.
Establishing the Buddha-dharma to protect the world, the Great Sage’s power and majesty are inconceivable;
he manifests a single dharma for swift transcendence.
Within that single dharma, he further manifests three divisions, each of which contains three distinct types; among these, the first is for the averting of calamities.
The brief explanation for the various sections on averting calamities is now complete; next, the rites for augmentation shall be explained.

Whether seeking long life and wealth, or desiring the gateway of intelligence and retention, or seeking knowledge of past lives to know what precedes and follows, or rejoicing in worldly power like that of a nāga—[these are the goals].
If one wishes to increase merit for oneself, one must first consume the "three white foods" at every meal.
If one seeks a long life free from ailment, one should construct a fire-pit in the shape of a lotus, measuring one cubit in depth, height, and circumference.
Furthermore, take the five pure substances and smear them within it.

Furthermore, take ghee, honey, and sandalwood; for each incantation, burn one portion while reciting your own name, repeating this one hundred and eight times, one thousand and eight times, or even up to three thousand times according to the preceding ritual.
Should there be extremely heavy karma from previous lives, it shall all be entirely eliminated without exceeding ten thousand repetitions.
Having extinguished sins, one increases merit and wisdom; One immediately attains freedom from illness and long life.
If one performs this rite for the sake of another, One should simply recite that person’s name, and the Dharma will act accordingly.
The practitioner should act according to the Dharma and maintain mindfulness, Taking willow wood every morning at dawn.

When the mantra has been completed eight hundred times, one should chew it. Before long—within one month or perhaps three months—one will be able to open the heart-mind and attain clarity of intellect.
For the performance of *homa*, one should recite the root great mantra with the *sūkṣma-mantra*. This brief explanation of mine serves to increase merit.
Quickly bestow your blessings upon sentient beings who lack merit; do not concern yourself with performing these various rites, but simply wish for long life and great protection of the body.
If one can recite [the mantra] one thousand and eight times every day, one will attain the supernormal power of knowing past lives in this very lifetime by practicing diligently day and night.

Whatever siddhi one seeks shall be accomplished without fail. Furthermore, if one seeks physical vigor and strength through the consumption of medicinal herbs, they should be empowered with the root mantra.
Once ten thousand recitations have been completed, one must take them on an empty stomach; this should be done for twenty-one, thirty-five, or even forty-nine days.
Their power is equal to that of the nine dragons, without distinction;
if one holds this, it is like the long-life elixir of immortality, whereby one may pass through a kalpa or even beyond a medium kalpa.
If one holds medicinal herbs to seek accomplishment, they surpass all other classes, and success is thereby attained—using such things as cow’s ghee, arsenic, and realgar.
One must hold a single object within the mandala; begin the recitation at the first watch of the night on either the first day of the waxing moon or the fifteenth.
Recite for one full period without interruption, until the three signs appear, which is the sole limit.
First, the sign of warmth appears, whereby one becomes wise and intelligent.
Second, the sign of smoke obscures the body; third, fire appears and ascends into the sky.
Having attained this, one becomes a great ṛṣi.
One should consume ghee from a sacrificial cow and apply medicines such as realgar to oneself. I have now finished explaining these rites for increase.
I shall now further explain the rites of compliance: for humans, non-humans, and animals alike.
Furthermore, take salt mixed with barley flour to fashion the desired form according to one's intent;
for a male, on the left, and for a female, on the right, beginning from the feet. One must use a blade of bin-iron to cut it finely.
Three times each day, one hundred and eight [times], up to one thousand and eight, according to one's own inclination;
if one wishes to perform a *rāśi* for the purpose of causing recollection, one should fashion an image, hold it, and recite its name.
One must also perform *homa* while mindful of the name; not exceeding eight hundred [recitations], it will accord with one's heart's desire.
If one wishes to subdue the nāgas and act in accordance with their nature: first, one should create a nāga resembling the form of a snake;
if seeking rain, it must be blue, and if during a flood, it should be red.
For the fire offering, one must use wood from milky trees; within no more than three days, success will be achieved.
In performing the rite, one must maintain a sincere intention; within it, one must not harbor a mind of indolence or arrogance.
If one intends to gather the various devas, yakṣas, and others, one should call each by their respective original name according to their kind.
If there are enemies, one may cause them to rejoice; by means of recitation, one can even transform their minds.
One may perform homa or engage in recitation; the distinctions between superior, middling, and inferior enemies are as follows:
for those of superior faculties and merit, three hundred recitations; for those of middling or inferior faculties lacking merit, one should repeat them accordingly.
I have briefly explained this according to one's own intention; the wise should reflect upon it with careful attention.
Completely encompassing all sections, the secret and most essential Lotus Heart—
I now bow my head to that Great Sage. For the sake of manifesting various skillful means to protect the Buddha-dharma,
he manifests in wrathful form to subdue and destroy those who harm the holy Dharma.
In this rite, the hearth must be triangular; Use wood from female trees along with damp fuel.
If performing this ritual, it must be during the dark fortnight, Or on the first day of the month.
Bare-bodied, delighting in solitude, and assuming a wrathful demeanor, Recite the mantra aloud while calling upon his name.
Cast foul butter and foul oil into the base of the hearth; without completing even a thousand and eight [recitations], one will naturally subjugate spirits and demons who are violent.
One should again burn *vilva* wood, or *nimba* wood, or fresh wood; then, mixing flour with human blood, fashion another image.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times over each section; within no more than three days, [the subject] will become compliant and gentle.

If, however, they remain unsubdued or destroy the Dharma, apply yourself with focused intent to making offerings to the Great Radiant King (*Mahāvidyārāja*), burning various poisonous substances in the hearth, and further perform *homa* using moist firewood.
Within three days, repeat [the mantra] eight hundred times to cause that evil person to immediately turn their mind [toward virtue].
Furthermore, if one does not perform the homa rite but wishes to subjugate all beings by reciting the root mantra,
one must call out the name of the target at every syllable.
When the count has again reached eight hundred recitations, he will come of his own accord and show respect.
According to the ritual, this subjugation is briefly explained:
the practitioner must contemplate with focused attention the profound and secret oral instructions, reciting them in sequence while fully concentrating the gates of the senses.
If one can serve this Honored One, it is not merely from having planted roots of goodness in a single lifetime;
rather, one must have previously attended upon immeasurable Buddhas and cultivated the ultimate gateway to enlightenment.
Furthermore, if within that process one encounters a virtuous friend, in a single lifetime one shall enter the indestructible gateway.
If I were to describe these merits in detail, I could praise them without end for immeasurable billions of kalpas;
now I have merely briefly set forth this small portion, a summary of the ritual manual of the Cintāmaṇicakra, for those practitioners who cultivate it with a focused and diligent mind.
